note:
Site-wide home for the layout overrides. footer-group renders on every page, so one style block serves every template — the homepage copy is removed in the same pass. Server-rendered CSS applies before first paint regardless of document position, so being in the footer causes no flash.

The fault: the theme sizes image-link-blocks by ITEMS PER ROW, not by fractions. At >=1400px `large` asks for 5 and `medium` for 6; at 1000-1399px `medium` asks for 5. A row holding fewer blocks than that leaves whole columns empty — 274px dead on the homepage's four-tile rows, worse on page.ingredients nav_creams (4 blocks at `medium` = 2 empty columns).

The rules count children and set items-per-row to match, so a 4-item row fills as 4 and a 5-item row as 5. Counting children rather than naming section ids means it keeps working when sections are renamed, and covers page.ingredients and page.skin-concerns without further edits. Floor is 1000px because that is where the theme switches to the items-per-row grid; below it the section is a horizontal scroll-area that must not be touched.

Added: a six-item multi-column row becomes a horizontal slider on desktop. Malcolm asked for a review slider; the theme gives a mobile scroller but unbleeds to a two-row grid on desktop. Overriding the grid restores the scroller. The span reset matters — items carry `span 3` from column_size, and without resetting it each tile spanned three auto-flow tracks at 1757px wide. Tested in the live browser before being written into the theme: 403px tiles, 3.3 visible, section height down from 1826px to 1022px.

The six-item multi-column slider rule was replaced by a media-with-text rule: the reviews went back to the approved image-left/quote-right layout, so the multi-column rule no longer applied and would have affected any other six-item multi-column row.

settings.html:
<style>
/* Skingenetix brand layout overrides — Claude Code, 2026-08-21.
   Additive only: sets custom properties the theme already exposes. No theme
   Liquid or CSS file is modified (.claude/rules/shopify.md rules 2 and 3).

   Link-block rows fill the full row width.
   The theme sizes these by items-per-row, so a row holding fewer blocks than
   the configured count leaves whole columns empty. Match the count to the
   blocks actually present. Children are counted rather than section ids named,
   so this survives renames and covers every template.
   Floor 1000px: below that the section is a horizontal scroll-area. */
@media screen and (min-width: 1000px) {
  .image-link-blocks:has(> .image-link-blocks__item:nth-child(4)):not(:has(> .image-link-blocks__item:nth-child(5))) {
    --image-link-blocks-items-per-row: 4 !important;
  }
  .image-link-blocks:has(> .image-link-blocks__item:nth-child(5)):not(:has(> .image-link-blocks__item:nth-child(6))) {
    --image-link-blocks-items-per-row: 5 !important;
  }
}
/* Review slider: six media-with-text items advance one at a time.
   .media-with-text is `display:grid; overflow:hidden` with one __item per block,
   so six blocks stack vertically. Overriding the grid to a single 100%-wide
   auto-flow track with scroll snapping turns that stack into Tatcha's one-at-a-time
   slider, without touching a theme file.
   Replaces an earlier multi-column rule: that turned the reviews into a row of six
   small tiles, which was the wrong layout — the approved one is image left, quote
   right, and only needed sliding adding. */
.media-with-text:has(> .media-with-text__item:nth-child(6)) {
  grid: auto / auto-flow 100% !important;
  overflow-x: auto !important;
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
}
.media-with-text:has(> .media-with-text__item:nth-child(6)) > .media-with-text__item {
  scroll-snap-align: start;
}
</style>
